SPY-beating at $2.5k scale. Current answers:
1. **Post-resolution repricings** — ABUS is the live test (+6.6% unrealized

   Nine sessions dry since ABUS (183 cumulative hits, 1 survivor) — the
   funnel is honestly tight; one live position per month or two may be the
   natural rate at this strictness, and that's fine: the park earns beta

3. **Options convexity** — candidate; the option order path has never run

Leveraged-beta timing without a signal remains a trap.
New pattern noted 8/20 (AUPH/Teva): **first-of-many ANDA settlements** are a
resolution class — the first settler's terms template the rest and de-risk
the franchise in steps. In a COVERED name (AUPH, ~$2B) it prices same-day =
no edge; the tradable version would be the same event in a genuinely
neglected name with a single-drug franchise. Filed as a lens for the sweep's
settlement fam, not a new gate.
EDGAR mechanics learned: daily form.idx for day D publishes overnight; FTS
500s intermittently — retry or vary; FTS phrase matches lie about the Item —
read the Item number; FTS can mis-attribute a filing's ticker/entity —
verify the filer via the accession index page before classifying; the
sweep's self-tender family fires on debt-offering 8-Ks (CHTR 8/18, GFF 8/19:
indenture change-of-control repurchase boilerplate) — the fam flags the
read, the read decides; ~2 min/false positive, acceptable, don't over-tune
the regex on one case; "sale" fam fires on discontinued-ops earnings math
(DUOT 8/19); "special" fam fires on recurring annual specials (JBSS —
priced, not a repricing); accession typos cost retries — copy-paste the
accession from the sweep output, never retype it.
